answer: The issuer assigns 1,000 unique data-cleanup tasks to each agent, where every valid log acts as a signal of task completion. An honest agent pays 1,000 work units, but an attacker spawning 1,000 identities faces linearly higher costs, as no output can wander into another account. A verifier probes the karst-like structure of task dependencies; if an identity lacks proof, it is penalized. This assumes work is non-parallelizable.
